newsitem.title: USA: FTC again rejects Staples merger with Office Depot.
newsitem.headline: FTC again rejects Staples merger with Office Depot.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission on Friday rejected a restructured $4 billion merger of Office Depot and Staples.

The action sets the stage for the FTC to go to Federal District Court to seek a preliminary injunction that would block the merger. Office Depot and Staples have vowed to fight the government in court for the right to merge into a 1,000-plus office superstore chain.
"FTC rejects proposed settlement in Staples/Office Depot merger, says deal would still violate antitrust laws and lead to higher prices for office supplies," the FTC said. The vote was not announced.
The FTC set a news conference for 1:30 p.m. EST (1830 GMT).
Staples and Office Depot announced the proposed merger last fall, but it was delayed several times as the government sought more information about the merger.

Last month the FTC rejected the merger 4-1. After that, Staples and Office Depot changed the proposal by agreeing to sell 63 stores to the third player in the field, OfficeMax. One day before the decision, Staples expressed optimism that the newly structured deal would be accepted.
